title: Portrait and Well
premise: Gideon Ravensworth's late-night call-in show becomes a conduit for the dead of Hollow Creek when listeners who died the previous week start phoning in, each asking him to 'write it down.' His obsessive documentation leads him to a 1974 disappearance case and an excavation site where workers have uncovered a door sealed from the inside. As Gideon investigates, he learns the town's founding families survived a lean winter by sealing eleven neighbors into a root cellar and taking their land, and that the dead will not rest until what was stolen is returned to the last living descendant of the sealed. The novel ends with Gideon signing the deed over at dawn, choosing to lose his own name and home so the dead can finally hang up.
about_author: Jonah Quintana is the pen name of a former small-town radio engineer who spent fifteen years maintaining transmitter towers across rural Appalachia before turning to fiction. He writes horror about towns that keep their ledgers balanced by any means necessary.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Gideon hosts his final broadcast from the failing AM station in Hollow Creek, where a caller named Marcy describes her own funeral from last Tuesday. He assumes a prank until two more dead callers phone in with details only they could know. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination—the thrill of being chosen, the first pull toward belonging.

chapters.title: The Ledger Habit
chapters.summary: Gideon transcribes every call into notebooks, treating documentation as prayer, while station manager Ruth warns him the FCC complaint letters are real and someone is listening. The dead callers begin repeating one phrase: 'the well remembers.' POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: compulsive devotion hardening into obsession; he cancels his move to the city without telling anyone.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Dara Okafor, foreman of the crew digging the new municipal well, whose team unearths a wooden door set in stone—sealed from the inside, scratched with fingernail grooves. That night her youngest worker quits after hearing knocking under the site. Emotional beat: professional skepticism cracking into dread; Dara refuses to leave because the overtime money means her family stays housed.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Four
chapters.summary: Gideon digs through county archives and finds eleven names erased from the 1974 census, all owned property now held by four founding families. A dead caller, old man Petrie, walks him through the winter the town 'shared' its food. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: horror of recognition—he realizes his beloved town was built on a locked door.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Gideon traces the sole living descendant of the sealed: Ada Voss, ninety-one, dying in a care facility, unaware she's heir to everything the founding families took. Meanwhile the excavation crew starts receiving phone calls from numbers that don't exist. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Dara decides Gideon's madness is the only map that explains her crew's terror.

chapters.title: Sign Here
chapters.summary: A lawyer representing the founding families offers Ada papers signing away her claim for a generous settlement, timed suspiciously with the excavation. The dead callers grow frantic: if Ada signs, the theft becomes legal forever. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: urgency and guilt—he understands he was given the calls because he's the only one who'll write it down.

chapters.title: Knocking
chapters.summary: The door at the well site begins opening inward a fraction each night despite fresh concrete poured around it. Dara's crew walks off; she alone stays, recording the sounds. The dead callers' voices merge into one chorus reciting the eleven names. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: solidarity with the trapped dead over her own survival instinct—the price of survival comes due.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Gideon confronts the four heirs on air, reading the 1974 ledger aloud live. Two hang up their phones mid-denial; one arrives at the studio with a shotgun and finds the doors already unlocked from inside. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: righteous fury curdling into fear as justice outside the law reveals itself as something older than law.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: At the well site, Gideon and Dara bring Ada in her wheelchair to the door, which stands open onto a cellar that shouldn't fit inside the hillside. The dead offer terms: the land returns to Ada's line, or the town joins them. Ada, lucid for the first time in years, asks Gideon why he never counted himself among the taken. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: terrible clarity—belonging has always meant being claimed.

chapters.title: Signing Papers
chapters.summary: Gideon signs the deed transferring his own house and name into Ada's restored estate, making himself the last resident who gives rather than takes. The door seals itself from the outside this time; the phones go quiet mid-sentence. Epilogue: Dara fills the well with clean water; a new voice calls the station asking for Gideon, and no one answers. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: grief braided with peace—the price paid, the ledger finally closed.
